{"metadata":{"description":"Vim keybindings for the deepseek-harness Web GUI, as an independent out-of-tree Cordis plugin","id":"gh:1333824391","install_available":false,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-vim-keymap","slug":"zijun1991/dsh-vim-keymap","topics":["cordis","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","keybindings","vim"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Vim keybindings for the deepseek-harness Web GUI, as an independent out-of-tree Cordis plugin"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-vim-keymap"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"**English** | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Vim keybindings for the deepseek-harness Web GUI, shipped as an independent, out-of-tree Cordis plug"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"in — it never modifies deepseek-harness itself."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Scope: vim-style keyboard assist, not a vim reimplementation"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"The goal here is narrow on purpose: let the composer and session tree be
driven from the keyboard th"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"e way vim habits already know, not reproduce vim
itself. The actual work in a deepseek-harness sessi"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"on — writing, editing,
searching, running things — is carried out by the agent, not by a human
doing"},{"id":"p6s4","text":" character-by-character text manipulation the way a real vim session
assumes; investing in vim's ful"},{"id":"p6s5","text":"l surface (registers, macros, marks,
jumplists, custom text objects, a real ex-command language) wou"},{"id":"p6s6","text":"ld spend
effort on capability nobody using this plugin is positioned to exercise."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"So new behavior gets added when it removes a specific, concrete keyboard
friction — Shift+Esc needin"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"g to reach Session mode even when focus has
drifted off the composer, a double-tapped Escape as a wa"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"y back in when
nothing else is listening, one `save` command that replaces a mouse click on
the host"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"'s "Session log" button — not to chase feature parity with a
`.vimrc`-grade vim setup. Normal mode's"},{"id":"p7s5","text":" text editing stays exactly what
`@replit/codemirror-vim` ships out of the box, unextended; Command "},{"id":"p7s6","text":"mode's
vocabulary staying at one command (see "Known limitations" below) is this
principle in practi"},{"id":"p7s7","text":"ce, not an oversight."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Modes"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"A small mode badge (bottom-right, non-interactive, reads `Vim Mode: <MODE>`)
shows which of the four"},{"id":"p10s2","text":" modes is live — the only visual cue for it, since
nothing in the host UI otherwise indicates vim st"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"ate. Its display policy —
`'persistent'` (always shown, the default), `'on-change'` (shown for ~1.2s"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"
after a transition, then hidden), or `'hidden'` — and the `enterNormal`/
`enterSession` shortcuts t"},{"id":"p10s5","text":"hemselves (default `Escape`/`Shift+Escape`) are all
user-editable through a "Vim Keymap" card this p"},{"id":"p10s6","text":"lugin registers into
Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration, backed by `localStorage` (see
"Setti"},{"id":"p10s7","text":"ngs persistence" below for why not the Host settings document).
`enterSession` is a global shortcut,"},{"id":"p10s8","text":" not scoped to the composer having focus
— see below."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"The Enter/send convention is enforced, not left to the host's own default:
confirmed against a real "},{"id":"p11s2","text":"running `dsh --profile web` instance that the
host's own bubble-phase handler treats a bare Enter as"},{"id":"p11s3","text":" "send" by default,
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"## Why this never touches deepseek-harness"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Every integration point is either an existing, general-purpose extension point, or driven off alread"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"y-public, already-rendered state:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"- **Normal mode** reaches the composer's `useInput`/`inputActions` by registering a headless (render"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"-nothing) component into `conversation.session.header.actions` — a `list`-kind slot `ui-conversation"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"` already declares for third-party header buttons. It never registers into `conversation.composer.ba"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"r` (InputBar's own exclusive slot) and never imports InputBar internals. Real text editing runs on a"},{"id":"p14s5","text":" headless `@codemirror/view` `EditorView` with `@replit/codemirror-vim`, never mounted to visible DO"},{"id":"p14s6","text":"M; edits flow back through `inputActions.setDraft()`, the same public write path InputBar itself use"},{"id":"p14s7","text":"s.
- **Session mode** never imports `ui-workspace` or its view store. It reads the workspace tree st"},{"id":"p14s8","text":"raight off the rendered, accessible DOM (`role="tree"`/`role="treeitem"`/`aria-expanded`) and drives"},{"id":"p14s9","text":" fold/expand and row-open by dispatching real `click` events on the row elements — the same thing a "},{"id":"p14s10","text":"mouse user does. `ui-workspace`'s internal store is never touched.
- **Command mode** portals into `"},{"id":"p14s11","text":"document.body`, and the whole plugin's global surface (the Session-mode overlay + Command palette + "},{"id":"p14s12","text":"mode badge) registers into `shell.overlay`, the additive global-overlay slot `ui-layout` documents f"},{"id":"p14s13","text":"or exactly this purpose.
- Both dynamically-declared slots (`conversation.session.header.actions`, s"},{"id":"p14s14","text":"cope `session`; `shell.overlay`, scope `root`) are reached through `ctx.slots.inject(key, factory)`,"},{"id":"p14s15","text":" not a direct `ctx.slots.register(...)` call — confirmed against a real running `dsh --profile web` "},{"id":"p14s16","text":"instance that a direct call races the owning plugin's own declaration and throws `slot "..." is not "},{"id":"p14s17","text":"declared` (the boot graph's per-package `inject` metadata is informational, not an activation-order "},{"id":"p14s18","text":"guarantee — see `packages/client/modules/src/client/manifest.ts`'s `WebBootEntry.inject` doc in deep"},{"id":"p14s19","text":"seek-harness). `ctx.slots.inject` is the pattern `ui-jobs`/`ui-subagent`/`ui-agent-preset` already u"},{"id":"p14s20","text":"se for the same slot."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Known limitations / follow-up work"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- **Command mode's vocabulary has exactly one command: `save` (normal flavor only).** It clicks the "},{"id":"p16s2","text":"host's own "Session log" button (the closest existing UI affordance to "save this session" — there i"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"s no `InputActions`/`SessionInput` verb for it; see `src/client/session/session-log-bridge.ts`), mat"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"ched by that button's visible text since it carries no `aria-label` and its CSS class is build-hashe"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"d. Everything else about the palette is still shell only (portal mount, flavor-specific styling, sub"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"mit/cancel keys) — this is deliberate scope, not an oversight (see "Scope" above): a session-flavor "},{"id":"p16s7","text":"command or a richer normal-flavor vocabulary is separate, concrete-need-driven work, not growth towa"},{"id":"p16s8","text":"rd a "complete" vim command set.
- **`focusSearch()` drives the real session-search input**, confirm"},{"id":"p16s9","text":"ed against a real running `dsh --profile web` instance: `ui-workspace`'s `WorkspaceBrowser.tsx` rend"},{"id":"p16s10","text":"ers it as a plain, always-present `<input type="text">` with no distinguishing `aria-label`/stable c"},{"id":"p16s11","text":"lass, starting visually collapsed (`opacity: 0`, `pointer-events: none`) until its sibling toggle bu"},{"id":"p16s12","text":"tton is clicked — a bare `.focus()` alone does nothing (confirmed live after an earlier false positi"},{"id":"p16s13","text":"ve from a stale prior click), so `src/client/workspace/tree-bridge.ts` clicks that toggle (found str"},{"id":"p16s14","text":"ucturally, as the input's only sibling carrying `aria-expanded` — locale/build-independent, unlike i"},{"id":"p16s15","text":"ts Chinese `aria-label`) before focusing. The one other `<input type="text">` seen on screen — the r"},{"id":"p16s16","text":"ename-workspace dialog's name field — only exists while that dialog's `role="dialog"` wrapper is mou"},{"id":"p16s17","text":"nted, which is what tells the two apart.
